parole.significato: The second letter of the Norwegian Bokmål alphabet, written in the Latin script.
parole.testo: From Latin B, from Etruscan 𐌁 (b, be), from Ancient Greek Β (B, beta), from the Phoenician 𐤁 (b, bet), from Proto-Canaanite , from Proto-Sinaitic , from Egyptian 𓉐, representing the plan of a house.

parole.significato: The second letter of the Norwegian Bokmål alphabet, written in the Latin script.
parole.testo: Modification of the capital letter B by dropping its upper loop, from Latin B, from Etruscan 𐌁 (b, “be”), from Ancient Greek Β (B, “beta”), from the Phoenician 𐤁 (b, “bet”), from Proto-Canaanite , from Proto-Sinaitic , from Egyptian 𓉐, representing the plan of a house.

parole.significato: The third letter of the Norwegian Bokmål alphabet, written in the Latin script.
parole.testo: From Latin C, from Etruscan Etruscan 𐌂 (c), from Ancient Greek Γ (G, gamma), from Phoenician 𐤂 (g, giml).

parole.significato: The third letter of the Norwegian Bokmål alphabet, written in the Latin script.
parole.testo: From Latin c, from the uppercase letter C, from Etruscan Etruscan 𐌂 (c), from Ancient Greek Γ (G, “Gamma”), from Phoenician 𐤂 (g, “gimel”).

parole.significato: The twentieth letter of the Norwegian Bokmål alphabet, written in the Latin script.
parole.testo: The uppercase form of t. From Latin T, from the Etruscan letter Etruscan 𐌕 (t, “te”), from Ancient Greek Τ (T, “tau”), itself borrowed from Phoenician 𐤕 (t, “taw; literally “mark, sign””), ultimately from the Egyptian hieroglyph Egyptian 𓏴 (“a pair of crossed sticks”).
